story.title: Cristiano Ronaldo Retires from International Football at Age 41
story.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football, concluding a career that spanned over two decades with the Portuguese national team. The announcement comes after a recent disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus regarding playing time. Ronaldo's international career included participation in six World Cups and a European Championship title.

explore_lenses.label: Will Ronaldo play for Portugal again?
explore_lenses.title: His final appearance is unclear
explore_lenses.summary: Ronaldo said he would give up Portugal’s No. 7 shirt after the November international break, but reporting differs on whether he will play in that break. UEFA lists Portugal’s remaining group matches against Denmark on November 14 and Wales on November 17.

claims.text: UEFA schedules Portugal to host Denmark on November 14, 2026, and to play Wales away on November 17; Portugal had already secured a Nations League quarterfinal place before those matches.
Ronaldo’s announcement said he would hand back the No. 7 shirt after the November international break, according to contemporaneous reporting.

Reporting is inconsistent on a farewell appearance: one account says the November matches could be his final chances to add to his totals, while another says his September 24 match against Wales was his last Portugal appearance.

explore_lenses.label: How did the dispute with Jorge Jesus unfold?
explore_lenses.title: A selection dispute became a public rupture
explore_lenses.summary: The break followed Ronaldo being left out against Norway and then leaving camp before Denmark. Ronaldo and Jorge Jesus offered materially different accounts of what had been agreed about his role.

claims.text: Ronaldo left Portugal’s camp after Jesus said he would not start him against Denmark; Ronaldo had been an unused substitute in the preceding 2-1 win over Norway.

Ronaldo’s account was that Jesus had agreed to manage his fitness by withholding him from the Norway and Denmark matches, then told him he would get 30 minutes against Norway but did not use him; Ronaldo described that as a broken promise.
Jesus said Ronaldo could return if he chose, while also framing selection around current performance rather than past achievements.

explore_lenses.label: What changes for Portugal on the field?
explore_lenses.title: Portugal must replace historic production
explore_lenses.summary: The retirement removes Portugal’s record appearance-maker and scorer, but the team has already secured a Nations League quarterfinal and has other forwards producing in the current campaign. The immediate tactical choice is Jesus’s, not a settled succession plan.

claims.text: Ronaldo leaves with 234 Portugal appearances and 146 goals, both men’s international records; his career included six World Cups and Portugal’s Euro 2016 title.

UEFA’s Portugal-Denmark squad listing names Gonçalo Ramos, João Félix, Rafael Leão, Francisco Conceição, Francisco Trincão, Pedro Neto and Fábio Silva among the forwards, but not Ronaldo; Ramos had three goals in four competition appearances in that listing.
The Portuguese Football Federation said it intends to organize a public tribute for Ronaldo, according to reporting that quoted its statement.

story_report.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has announced he is retiring from Portugal duty at 41, ending an international career that lasted more than two decades. The decision followed a public dispute with head coach Jorge Jesus over his role in the team. Ronaldo said he would relinquish Portugal’s No. 7 shirt after the November international break, while the national side prepares for scheduled Nations League matches against Denmark and Wales without a confirmed long-term successor for his leadership role or shirt number.

sections.heading: Ronaldo’s exit follows selection dispute
sections.body: Ronaldo left Portugal’s camp after Jesus said he would not start him against Denmark, following a 2-1 win over Norway in which Ronaldo was an unused substitute. Ronaldo said Jesus had previously agreed to manage his fitness by holding him out of the Norway and Denmark matches, then promised him 30 minutes against Norway but did not play him. The reviewed material does not independently establish that private agreement. Jesus said Ronaldo could return if he chose, but said selection should depend on current performance rather than past achievements.

sections.heading: Ronaldo leaves Portugal scoring records
sections.body: Ronaldo departs with 234 Portugal appearances and 146 goals, both men’s international records. His national-team career included six World Cups and Portugal’s Euro 2016 triumph. The Portuguese Football Federation intends to organize a public tribute, according to reporting that quoted its statement.

sections.heading: Portugal prepares for post-Ronaldo transition
sections.body: Portugal are scheduled to host Denmark on November 14 and play Wales away on November 17, having already secured a Nations League quarterfinal place. UEFA’s Portugal-Denmark squad listing included forwards such as Gonçalo Ramos, João Félix and Rafael Leão, but not Ronaldo; Ramos had scored three goals in four competition appearances in that listing. Reports conflict over whether Ronaldo could make a farewell appearance in November or whether his September 24 match against Wales was already his final Portugal outing.

unresolved.text: It had not been publicly resolved in the reviewed material whether Ronaldo would be selected or play in either November fixture.
No official long-term replacement for Ronaldo’s captaincy, role or No. 7 shirt was identified in the reviewed material.
